extracted.intended_audience: aspiring poets, critics, and readers of American poetry (late-19th-century democratic literary audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance on the qualities, attitudes, and practices that make a poet and a poem 'great' in the American democratic tradition; emphasizes candor, naturalism, universality, engagement with science and the age, and moral/esthetic seriousness. Intended as a handbook of aesthetic and ethical criteria for poets and critics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet as free channel (avoid marked style and artifice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The great poet has less a mark'd style, and is more the channel of thoughts and things without increase or diminution, and is the free channel of himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be meddlesome; avoid ornament, affected elegance, or contrivances that 'hang in the way' between poet and reader. 'What I tell I tell for precisely what it is.' Strive for directness so the reader 'stands by my side and look in the mirror with me.' Anti-pattern: stylistic tricks or artifice that draw attention to themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unconstraint and original practical example
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is finer than silent defiance advancing from new free forms; the greatest poet is he who contributes the greatest original practical example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value unconstrained innovation—new forms that arise from the poet's native impulse. Originality should be practical and demonstrable (an example others can follow), not merely eccentric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create your own suitable sphere
rubrics_metrics.description: The cleanest expression is that which finds no sphere worthy of itself, and makes one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If existing forms do not fit your expression, fashion a new form or context rather than forcing your content into ill-suited conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusiveness and equality of address
rubrics_metrics.description: The messages of great poems to each man and woman are, Come to us on equal terms, only then can you understand us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poems should address readers as equals and be accessible across classes, sexes, and conditions. Avoid elitism or exclusionary postures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation of individual greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: We affirm there can be unnumber'd Supremes ... men can be good or grand only of the consciousness of their supremacy within them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry should celebrate the individual's inner sense of greatness—uplift and empower the reader to recognize their own worth and capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generosity and encouragement toward competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: The American bards shall be mark'd for generosity and affection, and for encouraging competitors. They shall be Kosmos, without monopoly or secrecy, glad to pass anything to any one--hungry for equals night and day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate an open, sharing stance toward fellow writers; do not hoard techniques or knowledge. Encourage rivals rather than suppress them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indifference to material riches; inner affluence
rubrics_metrics.description: They shall not be careful of riches and privilege--they shall be riches and privilege--they shall perceive who the most affluent man is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poets should prize inner wealth and expressive riches over social status or material accumulation. Anti-pattern: seeking poetry as a route to conventional privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-partisanship across regions and classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The American bard shall delineate no class of persons ... and not be for the Eastern States more than the Western, or the Northern States more than the Southern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid regionalism, class favoritism, or sectional biases; poetry should speak for the whole democratic nation rather than particular cliques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with exact science and practical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Exact science and its practical movements are no checks on the greatest poet, but always his encouragement and support. ... the anatomist, chemist, astronomer, geologist ... are not poets, but they are the lawgivers of poets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate scientific knowledge and empirical observation—the sciences supply concepts, structures, and seeds of poetic thought. Treat scientific fact as an ally, not an enemy, of poetic imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalism; rejection of miraculous violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole theory of the supernatural ... departs as a dream. ... They are sufficient for any case and for all cases -- any special miracle of affairs or persons inadmissible in the vast clear scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on miraculous interventions or supernatural contrivances in poetry; adhere to the 'vital laws' and intelligible natural processes. Anti-pattern: invoking miracles to solve poetic or moral problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candid investigation of people and nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Men and women, and the earth and all upon it, are to be taken as they are, and the investigation of their past and present and future shall be unintermitted, and shall be done with perfect candor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain frank, honest observation and reporting of experience and fact; candid depiction is central to poetic truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy grounded in tendencies toward happiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The eternal tendencies of all toward happiness make the only point of sane philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry and speculative thought should orient toward human flourishing and the tendencies that promote well-being; avoid systems that ignore or deny this orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid portraying God as opposing natural law
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever would put God in a poem or system of philosophy as contending against some being or influence, is also of no account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid theological constructions in poetry that depict the divine as at odds with observable reality or human nature; favor immanent, life-affirming religious feeling rather than conflictual metaphysics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political liberty as indispensable poetic attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: In the make of the great masters the idea of political liberty is indispensable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry should embody and sustain the ideal of liberty; poets are voices of and custodians for freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuineness over fiction and romance
rubrics_metrics.description: As the attributes of the poets of the kosmos ... they possess the superiority of genuineness over all fiction and romance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor truthfulness and authentic depiction rather than contrived romanticism; factual illumination enhances poetic power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid grotesque distortion and unearthly ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: That which distorts honest shapes, or which creates unearthly beings or places or contingencies, is a nuisance and revolt. Of the human form especially, it is so great it must never be made ridiculous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ornament must not distort natural forms. Avoid monstrous exaggerations and fanciful inventions that betray natural truth. Acceptable ornament must 'conform to the perfect facts of the open air' and arise inevitably from the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ornament must flow from nature; minimal ornament preferred
rubrics_metrics.description: Of ornaments to a work nothing outre can be allow'd--but those ornaments can be allow'd that conform to the perfect facts of the open air, and that flow out of the nature of the work ... Most works are most beautiful without ornament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ornament sparingly and only when it is a natural outgrowth of the subject; prefer simplicity and let the work stand without superfluous embellishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exaggeration; favor natural models
rubrics_metrics.description: Exaggerations will be revenged in human physiology. Clean and vigorous children are jetted and conceiv'd only in those communities where the models of natural forms are public every day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist hyperbole and caricature; cultivate natural, healthful models in life and art. Excessive exaggeration harms both art and society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of tricks; perfect personal candor
rubrics_metrics.description: The great poets are to be known by the absence in them of tricks, and by the justification of perfect personal candor. All faults may be forgiven of him who has perfect candor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not employ rhetorical or deceptive 'tricks.' Radical honesty of voice and intention is the highest redeeming quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute honesty; do not lie
rubrics_metrics.description: Henceforth let no man of us lie, for we have seen that openness wins the inner and outer world ... the soul has never once been fool'd and never can be fool'd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poets must practice truthfulness in life and art; openness and honesty are both ethical and esthetic imperatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence in the larger sense (health, compassion, social wisdom)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extreme caution or prudence, the soundest organic health, large hope and comparison and fondness for women and children ... are called up ... to be parts of the greatest poet from his birth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate robust physical and moral health, broad hope, and care for family and community; prudence here means sustaining life's fullness rather than narrow thrift aimed only at accumulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence directed to immortality rather than mere gain
rubrics_metrics.description: The prudence of the mere wealth and respectability ... appears too faint ... The prudence suitable for immortality ... The prudence of the greatest poet answers at last the craving and glut of the soul ... has no particular sabbath or judgment day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value long-term spiritual and artistic prudence—actions that nourish the soul and posterity—over short-term financial security or respectability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be the age; intensely engage the present
rubrics_metrics.description: The direct trial of him who would be the greatest poet is to-day. If he does not flood himself with the immediate age ... let him merge in the general run, and wait his development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absorb and transmute contemporary life—its currents, events, sciences, and sensibilities—into poetry. Failure to engage the present risks irrelevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescience and endurance: judge by centuries
rubrics_metrics.description: The prescient poet projects himself centuries ahead, and judges performer or performance after the changes of time. Does it live through them? Does it still hold on untired?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create with an eye toward longevity; the true test is whether work remains vital across generations and still speaks to young and old alike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality across sexes, ages, classes
rubrics_metrics.description: A great poem is for ages and ages in common, and for all degrees and complexions, and all departments and sects, and for a woman as much as a man, and a man as much as a woman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for broad human appeal and relevance—avoid catering only to narrow audiences or ephemeral fashions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry should provoke action and new seeing, not comfort
rubrics_metrics.description: A great poem is no finish to a man or woman, but rather a beginning ... The touch of him, like Nature, tells in action ... Whom he takes he takes with firm sure grasp into live regions previously unattain'd ... and shall never be quiet again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft poetry that transforms perception and propels readers into continued thought and action rather than offering final consolations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poets as secular priests inspired by real objects
rubrics_metrics.description: There will soon be no more priests. ... A new order shall arise, and they shall be the priests of man ... They shall find their inspiration in real objects to-day, symptoms of the past and future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the cultural role of moral and aesthetic leadership while grounding inspiration in concrete, contemporary reality rather than ecclesiastical dogma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of English for robust, democratic expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The English language befriends the grand American expression--it is brawny enough, and limber and full enough ... It is the chosen tongue to express growth, faith, self-esteem, freedom, justice, equality, friendliness, amplitude, prudence, decision, and courage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ English as a flexible, powerful medium suited to expressing democratic and vigorous American themes; favor clarity and strength of diction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity with American democratic standards and usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it uniform with my country? Are its disposals without ignominious distinctions? Is it for the ever-growing communes of brothers and lovers, large, well united, proud ... Is it for the nursing of the young of the republic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate work by whether it serves democratic community, resists ignominious distinctions, and nurtures future generations. Literature should contribute to the republic's moral and aesthetic growth.
